selection: Purposive exploratory batch; cannot estimate prevalence.

cases.title: Seattle Pioneer Square areaways

claims.locator: Main-text paragraphs defining areaways and describing street raising
claims.statement: SDOT reports engineered street raising after the 1889 fire and retaining walls beneath roadways.

cases.physical_evidence: No site inspection or sediment sample. Municipal maintenance account describes below-sidewalk spaces and a supporting street wall.
cases.surviving_documents: Modern SDOT account; original grading plans uncollected.
cases.source_interpretation: Deliberate grade raising created the lower level.
cases.investigation_inference: An identified engineering alternative merits checking against original records before attributing burial to a natural event.
competing_explanations: Local natural deposition or subsidence, if independently evidenced
cases.counterevidence: The below-ground level alone does not discriminate its cause; an engineered mechanism is documented.
cases.next_test: Retrieve block-specific grading plans and dated construction records; compare wall geometry and fill logs.

chronology.dated_object: Street raising as reported in a modern account

cases.dependence: Same city as C002, but a different project; do not merge dates or count city-level narratives as independent global observations.

cases.title: Denny Hill regrade archival collection

claims.locator: Scope and Contents and Dates fields
claims.statement: The finding aid describes earthmoving and a photograph collection created in 1904-1929.

cases.physical_evidence: No image or site directly inspected.
cases.surviving_documents: Engineering photograph collection located through its finding aid.
cases.source_interpretation: The catalog attributes terrain changes to a regrade project.
cases.investigation_inference: Provides a route to original evidence of human terrain change, not a verified image sequence yet.
competing_explanations: An earlier natural event, separately testable
cases.counterevidence: A regrade catalog cannot be recast as a catastrophe deposit without examining the underlying objects.
cases.next_test: Inspect identified photographs and engineering quantities; record individual identifiers and phases.
cases.dependence: Related urban context to C001. Shared archival narratives are not independent global-event evidence.

cases.title: High Arctic camel-bearing deposits

claims.statement: The paper reports a camel-bearing terrestrial deposit, fossil trees, and a mid-Pliocene context using cosmogenic dating.

cases.physical_evidence: Fossils and deposits reported by researchers; no specimen or full dating table inspected here.
cases.surviving_documents: 2013 research paper located; supplementary material unreviewed.
cases.source_interpretation: Authors reconstruct a past warm-period forest environment.
cases.investigation_inference: Tests must compare fossil/host-layer ages before relating this locality to any historical catastrophe.
competing_explanations: Reworking or later transport if supported by contextual evidence
cases.counterevidence: The available reported geological context challenges an automatic recent-date interpretation.
cases.next_test: Inspect burial-dating methods/tables, error terms, site coordinates, stratigraphy and specimen identification.

chronology.reported: Mid-Pliocene; exact numerical bounds not entered
chronology.dated_object: Host deposits/context, not an inspected direct camel death date

cases.dependence: Nature and PMC are mirrors of the same study, not independent dating results.

cases.title: Cascadia tsunami and coastal subsidence
cases.place: Salmon River estuary, Oregon; wider Cascadia

claims.locator: Indexed research summary: sediment cores and subsidence paragraphs
claims.statement: USGS reports over 200 cores, tsunami sand and coastal subsidence assigned to the 1700 event.
A 2005 research report addresses Japanese clues to the 1700 event.

cases.physical_evidence: Reported core/deposit observations; no raw logs inspected.
cases.surviving_documents: USGS report located; original Japanese records unreviewed.
cases.source_interpretation: The research summary attributes local sediment and subsidence to an earthquake and tsunami.
cases.investigation_inference: A positive catastrophic-process comparison. Worldwide extent and fabrication require additional evidence.
competing_explanations: Other local inundation processes to compare using deposits
cases.counterevidence: A regional event does not establish simultaneous global burial.
cases.next_test: Read core logs and original historical records; audit their dating linkage and modeled inundation.

chronology.method: Underlying cross-disciplinary dating not audited here

cases.dependence: The modern summary and its underlying study overlap; publication metadata adds no independent event measurement.

cases.title: California-as-island map
cases.place: California/Baja California as depicted in a manuscript map

claims.statement: A cataloged map depicts California as an island and is dated approximately 1650.
The exhibition explains island depictions as geographic error and captions a 1639 map.

cases.physical_evidence: No original scan or geological transect inspected.
cases.surviving_documents: Map catalog and separate exhibition interpretation.
cases.source_interpretation: Curators describe a propagated geographic misconception.
cases.investigation_inference: Audit map lineages and physical coast evidence; do not treat drawn water as a surveyed former strait.
competing_explanations: A former waterway if independently evidenced
cases.counterevidence: The two source dates must not be fused until item identity is established.
cases.next_test: Inspect map scans/identifiers, related editions and exploration records; define a geological transect.
cases.dependence: Copied maps can share a single error. Catalog and exhibit are not independent coastal measurements.

cases.title: Eiffel Tower construction photograph lead

claims.statement: The museum catalogs a view described as tower construction on 10 February 1888.

cases.investigation_inference: Useful evidence lead; incomplete for deciding original build versus repair or inheritance.
competing_explanations: Repair/reassembly if fabric and earlier records support it
cases.counterevidence: No visual sequence, authenticated provenance, or construction budget has yet been examined.
cases.next_test: Inspect original images and provenance; trace dated drawings, fabrication, delivery, workforce and foundation phases.
cases.dependence: A museum caption alone is one attribution, not independent corroboration.

cases.title: Edison electric-lamp patent 223,898
cases.place: United States patent; Menlo Park attribution

claims.locator: PDF pages 2-3: heading, opening, antecedent discussion and claims
claims.statement: The scan identifies an 1879 application and an 1880 patent for an improvement; it discusses earlier incandescent lamps.
Metadata gives filing 4 November 1879 and publication 27 January 1880.

cases.physical_evidence: Patent scan visually inspected; no lamp tested.
cases.surviving_documents: Specification, claims and signature; notebooks unreviewed.
cases.investigation_inference: A priority audit must distinguish incremental improvement, first discovery, commercialization and recovered technology.
competing_explanations: Recovery from a demonstrably earlier artifact
cases.counterevidence: A patent alone proves neither sole invention nor recovery from a lost civilization.
cases.next_test: Compare antecedent patents, notebooks and working designs; require a dated access chain for any recovery claim.
cases.dependence: Scan and transcription are the same patent, not independent inventions.

cases.title: Missoula flood sequence
cases.place: Columbia River basin, northwest United States

claims.locator: Hosted summary: stratigraphic and chronology paragraphs
claims.statement: The review reports catastrophic landforms, repeated flood beds and intervening indicators of elapsed time.
The older report describes varves between successive graded flood beds.

cases.physical_evidence: Published geomorphic/stratigraphic observations; no field section inspected.
cases.investigation_inference: Catastrophic processes are a valid comparison; evidence of intervals tests a single-episode version.
competing_explanations: One episode only if intervening time indicators are convincingly reinterpreted
cases.counterevidence: Intervening time indicators challenge treating the whole sequence as one uninterrupted event.
cases.next_test: Inspect measured sections, tephra relations, dates and varve criteria; test separate-event alternatives quantitatively.

chronology.reported: Last-glacial sequence; precise dated sample intervals not entered
chronology.method: Reported multiple methods; not individually reanalyzed

cases.dependence: Review incorporates earlier research; do not count the review as a fresh independent field dataset.
